objective: Expose the completed ADR authoring/indexing convention to the future I-004 owner without creating concurrent writes in the Nx to Graph IR extractor scope.
context: The repository owner assigned I-004 to Claude and G-005 to Codex as separate work streams.

G-005 creates docs/adr/TEMPLATE.md and updates docs/adr/README.md only; it does not edit Graph IR generators, generated graph files, Nx configuration, CI, the master source, or current planning state.
The owner explicitly requires ADRs to appear later in the Architecture Studio review and test application.
criteria: Keep TEMPLATE.md outside ADR discovery; actual ADRs match ADR-[0-9]{4}-[a-z0-9-]+.md.
When ADR extraction is implemented, derive adr:<repository-relative-path>, source evidence, and content hash rather than treating the application projection as authority.
Use only active Graph IR relation kinds: Supersedes maps to supersedes; Amends and Related map to related_to until a versioned schema changes.
If I-004 updates canonical planning files, record G-005 as completed there instead of requiring Codex to edit the same shared files concurrently.
constraints: Do not rewrite this immutable handoff.
I-004 remains owned by Claude; this handoff does not transfer implementation scope.
The browser application consumes derived Graph IR and links to authored Markdown; it must not parse ADRs as a second architectural authority.
No X6 layout, viewport, color, or interaction concept belongs in ADR metadata or Graph IR.
uncertainties: I-004 currently targets Nx projects, targets, and edges; full ADR extraction may remain an I-006 or later extractor extension as long as the published authoring contract is preserved.
Existing ADRs retain their historical metadata shapes and will need explicit compatibility handling when ADR extraction is implemented.
return_schema: No response is required unless I-004 needs to change the G-005 files or cannot preserve the documented ADR indexing contract.
